claim: James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) itself is free to walk on and open 08:00-17:00, but tours from Phuket/Krabi typically include the separate Ao Phang Nga National Park fee; site is notoriously crowded so early-morning or late-afternoon visits are advised.
quote: James Bond Island can get quite crowded with tourists, especially during peak seasons. It is advisable to visit early in the morning or later in the afternoon to avoid large crowds.

claim: Phang Nga Bay is reached by speedboat (~45 min from Ao Po Grand Marina / Royal Phuket Marina), longtail (~1.5 h from Phang Nga pier), or sea canoe; group tours run 1,500-2,500 THB, premium kayak tours ~3,950 THB, private charters 8,000+ THB, with a 300 THB national park entrance for foreign adults.
quote: Group tours: 1,500-2,500 Baht per person ... Premium kayak tours (John Gray Sea Canoe): ~3,950 Baht ... National park entrance: 300 Baht (foreign adults)

claim: John Gray's flagship 10-hour 'Hong by Starlight' tour (฿3,950 pp, hotel pickup ~10:20-11:15 with departure from Ao Po pier at noon) explores hongs at Panak and Hong islands, views James Bond Island from the escort boat, and finishes with bioluminescent plankton after dark.
quote: The caves and hidden lagoons John Gray found in 1989 are explored during the tour

claim: Hongs are collapsed-cave interior lagoons enclosed by 100m limestone walls; the main Koh Hong lagoon is ~100m across, Koh Panak holds several hongs connected by sea caves, and many entries are tide-gated.
quote: Most hidden lagoons can only be entered during specific tidal conditions when the water level is just right—too high and the cave entrance is submerged, too low and kayaks scrape against rocky bottoms

claim: Koh Panyee is a stilt-built Muslim fishing village founded ~200 years ago by Javanese families, now home to roughly 400 families, famous for three floating soccer fields built after 1986 and reachable in 30 min by boat from Phang Nga Pier (~200 THB direct) or as a stop on James Bond Island tours.
quote: Pork, drinking alcohol and smoking is prohibited on Koh Panyee.

claim: Ice Cream Cave, named for its smooth dripping-stalactite ceiling, is reached only by inflatable canoe through a narrow entrance and floods at high tide, making it tide-window dependent; it is a regular stop on full-day Phang Nga Bay canoe tours.
quote: The cave gets its name from the smooth, melting-like texture of the stalactites hanging from its ceiling, resembling scoops of ice cream frozen in mid-drip.

claim: The Krabi-side Koh Hong (Mu Ko Hong) is a separate island from the Phang Nga Bay hong stops — about 20 min by boat from Ao Nang, with tours typically departing Nopparat Thara Pier and picking up at Ao Nang, Railay, Klong Muang and Tubkaek.
quote: There is another Hong Island in nearby Phang Nga Bay which is a popular kayaking stop on the Phang Nga Bay and James Bond Island tours. Make sure to check which islands you will be visiting before you book!

claim: Recent (Nov 2025) visitor reports price James Bond Island day tours at 1,300-2,500 THB depending on vessel, with hotel pickups around 07:00 from Rawai and return by 17:30; longtail boats are cheaper than speedboats and often combine temple or glass-bridge stops.
quote: The experience was affordable, action-packed, and absolutely worth it.

claim: Independent travellers can drive to Surakul Pier in Takua Thung (~12 km west of Phang Nga town) or Phang Nga Bay Harbour and hire a private longtail for roughly 1,500-2,500 THB for a 3-4 hour trip, bypassing big group tours from Phuket.
quote: You can drive to Surakul Pier or Phang Nga Bay Harbour to join any longtail boat.

claim: Foreign-adult park entry to Khao Sok's Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam zone is 300 baht (children 3-14 or under 140cm: 150 baht), raised from 200/100 baht effective 1 May 2024 and still in force for 2026.
quote: Effective Date: May 1st, 2024 ... Adults: 300 baht to access the Ratchaprapha Dam area ... Children (ages 3-14 or under 140cm): 150 baht ... foreign adult fees increased from 200 baht to 300 baht

claim: Cheow Lan Lake activities are bundled into mostly all-inclusive raft-house stays covering boat transfer from the pier, meals, kayaks/SUPs and guided wildlife boat safaris, with three signature caves (Coral, Pra Khie Phet ~30 min each, and the more adventurous Nam Talu).
quote: Cave exploration includes three main caves: Coral Cave and Pra Khie Phet (approximately 30 minutes each) and Nam Talu (more adventurous, involving water wading) ... Most stays are all inclusive: boat transfer from the pier to the lake house, all meals during the stay and activities.

claim: Khao Sok hosts gibbons, macaques, hornbills, slow lorises and occasional wild elephants, with nearly 400 bird species; February-May (dry season) gives the best chance of seeing elephants, hornbills, gibbons and langurs at the lake.
quote: Khao Sok is home to gibbons, macaques, hornbills, slow lorises, and occasionally wild elephants. There are nearly 400 bird species reported in Khao Sok National Park ... For the best chance of spotting wild elephants, hornbills, gibbons, and langurs, visit during dry season in February to May.

claim: Rafflesia kerrii, the giant parasitic flower endemic to southern Thailand and Khao Sok, blooms seasonally usually from January to March.
quote: Rafflesias flower seasonally usually from January to March ... Rafflesia kerrii is found in Khao Sok and the southern part of Thailand.

claim: The Rafflesia trek is a ~4-hour, 5-10 km jungle hike priced at ฿1,200 per person, bookable only on arrival because operators cannot guarantee a bloom on any given day (each flower lasts only days).
quote: 4 hours total ... guide you through the jungle for about 5-10km, in search of these wonderful flowers ... ฿1,200 per person ... we cannot guarantee that you will see the flowers in bloom

claim: Floating-bungalow pricing in 2026 spans roughly $80-100/night for budget eco rafts, ~$100-180 for mid-range Panvaree Resort, $250-400 for honeymoon-oriented Panvaree The Greenery, and $300-600+ at the luxury 500 Rai Floating Resort.
quote: 500 Rai Khao Sok Floating Resort ... Price: $300-$600+ per night ... Panvaree Resort ... $100-$180 per night ... Panvaree The Greenery ... $250-$400 per night ... Khao Sok Eco Raft ... $80-$100 per night

claim: Nam Talu cave is reached via a 2.5 km, 2-3 hour jungle trek and stretches ~700 m with waist-deep wading sections; it can be deadly in heavy rain after a 2007 flash flood killed eight people, so it is closed during the wet months.
quote: Nam Talu Cave stretches over approximately 700 meters ... trek through the jungle crossing small streams on a 2.5 kilometer route taking about 2 to 3 hours ... in a tragic 2007 incident, two guides and six tourists lost their lives in a sudden flash flood.

claim: Kayaking on the Sok River near the park HQ is a standout dry-season activity, with guides commonly spotting monkeys, otters and snakes along the banks.
quote: Kayaking activities are available with a local navigating the kayak, where visitors can see monkeys, otters and snakes. It's the best time of year for river kayaking, as the water levels drop in the dry season.

claim: Day-trippers from Khao Lak (about 1 hour from the village) are typically collected at 08:00 by minivan to Ratchaprapha Pier for a 4-6 hour longtail loop past the 'Guilin of Thailand' three-peak karsts, with cave visit, bamboo raft and lunch.
quote: Pick-up times from Khao Lak are at 08:00 AM, with transfers by private minivan to the Cheow Lan Dam Municipal Pier ... the longtail boat ride explores the limestone mountains of Ratchaprapha Dam and visits the 'Guilin of Thailand' area with three pointed limestone mountains.

claim: Cheow Lan Lake was created in 1982 when the Ratchaprapha Dam flooded a limestone valley; the resulting 165 km² reservoir, ringed by 900+ m karst peaks, is the centrepiece of the park's eastern (Phang Nga-accessible) sector.
quote: the lake was created in 1982 when the Ratchaprapha Dam was constructed, submerging a vast area of lush jungle and limestone cliffs

claim: Mu Ko Similan National Park's 2025-2026 season closes to all visitors on May 15, 2026 and remains shut for the monsoon.
quote: Similan Islands will close May 15th 2026

claim: Mu Ko Similan reopened for the 2025-2026 season on 15 October 2025.
quote: Similan Islands National Park Opening Season Phang Nga Thailand - 15 October 2025

claim: Both Mu Ko Similan and Mu Ko Surin national parks close 16 May to 14 October each year for ecological recovery.
quote: Similan and Surin Islands in Phang Nga Temporarily Closed for Ecological Recovery

claim: Foreign adult entrance fee for Mu Ko Similan and Mu Ko Surin is 500 baht (250 baht for children) under DNP Category 4.
quote: Category 4 covers Mu Koh Similan National Park and Mu Koh Surin National Park in Phang-nga. Foreign adults: 500 baht

claim: Optimal Similan visiting window is November-April with calm seas and best visibility; speedboat day trips from Thap Lamu pier take ~1.5-2 hours.
quote: Similan Islands Open Season 2025-2026: Best Time to Visit, Weather by Month & Tour Tips

claim: Day-trippers reach only the closer Similan sites while liveaboards access better outer reefs plus Koh Bon, Koh Tachai and Richelieu Rock.
quote: the nearer sites are worse as that is where the day trippers can reach

claim: Richelieu Rock is a horseshoe pinnacle ~40 km off the mainland, ranked among Asia's top sites and Thailand's premier whale-shark spot.
quote: Richelieu Rock - One of the best dive sites in Asia

claim: Koh Bon is Thailand's hot spot for manta rays and Koh Tachai pinnacle is one of the region's top quality dive sites; February-April is peak whale-shark season.
quote: Richelieu Rock, Koh Tachai/Bon Diving, Andaman Sea - Thailand

claim: Surin Islands tours typically include a visit to the Moken sea-gypsy village on Ko Surin, home to semi-nomadic people who traditionally lived on kabang boats.
quote: Moken Village: A Hidden Gem of the Surin Islands

claim: Surin's reefs are widely considered the healthiest in Thailand with sheltered bays ideal for beginner snorkellers; clownfish and turtles are common in shallow water.
quote: the colorful coral reefs scattered throughout the marine park, widely considered the healthiest in all of Thailand

claim: Police Boat 813, swept ~2 km inland by the 2004 tsunami while protecting Prince Bhumi Jensen, sits in Bang Niang as a free memorial open daily 08:30-18:00.
quote: dragged around 2 kilometres inland by the powerful tsunami waves, to where it rests now on dry land in Bang Niang

claim: Bang Niang Night Market on Phetkasem Road (opposite Police Boat 813) operates Mon/Wed/Thu/Sat ~16:00-22:00 with street food and crafts.
quote: Bang Niang Tourist Market - Khao Lak Center

claim: Coconut Beach sits inside national-park land so no engine boats or sunbeds are permitted, giving it a quiet, romantic atmosphere with shaded palms.
quote: Coconut Beach Khao Lak - Tranquil Tropical Paradise

claim: Pak Weep Beach, north of Coconut Beach, is spacious, quiet and good for swimming and walking with low development.
quote: Pak Weep Beach Khao Lak | Family-Friendly & Relaxing

claim: Khuk Khak Beach sits between Bang Niang and Pakarang with golden sand framed by pine woodlands and quick access to restaurants and markets.
quote: Khuk Khak Beach Khao Lak - Quiet Beach & Cozy Bars

claim: Nang Thong is Khao Lak's most popular beach: ~3 km long with space to spread out; Bang Niang is the main hub for bars, restaurants and sunsets.
quote: Nang Thong Beach is probably Khao Lak's most popular beach

claim: Pakarang Beach is shallow with coral patches so poor for swimming but lively for surfing and beach bars, second only to Bang Niang in atmosphere.
quote: this beach is the liveliest in Khao Lak after Bang Niang beach

claim: Diving the Similan, Koh Bon, Koh Tachai and Richelieu Rock circuit runs roughly mid-October through early May, with most liveaboards being 4-day/4-night trips from Khao Lak.
quote: Diving The Similan Islands 2026: A Quick Guide

claim: Wat Suwan Khuha (Monkey Cave Temple) sits ~10km south of Phang Nga Town in a limestone cave housing a 15-metre reclining golden Buddha, ancient chedis, and resident macaques; entry is roughly 20 baht and the temple opens 8am-5pm.
quote: The temple is best known for its impressive 15-meter-long reclining golden Buddha. The cave also houses smaller Buddha images and ancient chedis... open daily from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The entrance fee is very low (around 20 Baht).

claim: Visitors are warned that the cave's monkeys snatch sunglasses, water bottles and snacks, and arriving before 9:30am beats the Phang Nga Bay tour buses that pour in 10:30-noon.
quote: the monkeys are known to be curious and quick to snatch unattended items like sunglasses, water bottles, or even snacks... Arrive before 9:30 to have the cave largely to yourself.

claim: Wat Tham Tapan (Heaven and Hell Temple) on the edge of Phang Nga town is entered through an enormous dragon's mouth and contains graphic dioramas of Buddhist hell punishments; admission is free, hours 8:30am-6pm, and not recommended for young children.
quote: the open mouth of a massive dragon sculpture, symbolizing the entrance... The complex specifically depicts Na Rok, the Buddhist hell, populated with disturbing statues in torturous poses... Daily, 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM

claim: Sa Nang Manora Forest Park, a 15-minute drive north of Phang Nga town, has a free 2km nature trail through shaded jungle past cascades, a bat cave and swimmable waterfall pools.
quote: an easy to follow 2km nature trail through the park and it is permitted to swim in the waterfall pools... Entry to the park is free

claim: Takua Pa Old Town's Sunday Walking Street runs along the Sino-Portuguese shophouse strip on Sri Takua Pa Road, serving southern Thai snacks, grilled seafood and sweet roti to a mix of locals and visitors.
quote: Visitors can sample southern Thai snacks, grilled seafood, sweet roti, and fresh fruit... well-preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, a legacy of its tin mining past.

claim: Takua Pa, originally the spice-trading port of Takola, became a tin-dredging boomtown drawing Chinese, Dutch, Portuguese and British merchants; when tin prices collapsed in the 1900s the foreigners left but the Chinese community stayed and shaped the surviving Sino-Portuguese streetscape.
quote: an important tin dredging area, attracting diverse populations including Chinese migrants and Dutch, Portuguese, and British merchants... tin prices began to fall in the 1900s... While traders departed, the Chinese population remained and integrated into local society.

claim: Thailand ranked among the world's top tin exporters from 1967 to 1984, with Takua Pa's mines a key contributor; the district was renamed after takua, the Thai word for lead, despite tin being the more important ore.
quote: from 1967 to 1984 always ranked among the world's top tin exporters... takua (ตะกั่ว) is the Thai word for lead, even though tin was the most important ore found there.

claim: Most visits to Koh Panyee come as a stop on Phang Nga Bay speedboat or longtail tours alongside James Bond Island and Hong Island; modest dress is requested as the village is predominantly Muslim.
quote: guided speedboat tour from Phuket that includes stops at James Bond Island, Hong Island... Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) and be polite to residents—this is a predominantly Muslim fishing village.

claim: The Moken are an Austronesian sea-nomad people of the Mergui and Surin archipelagos who traditionally lived aboard kabang houseboats; since the 2004 tsunami the Thai government has required the Surin Moken to live in one settlement at Ao Bon on Ko Surin Tai.
quote: Since the tsunami of 2004, the Thai government has mandated that the Moken people of the Surin Islands reside in a single settlement, Ao Bon Bay, on Ko Surin Tai

claim: The Moken's most sacred ritual is the twice-yearly Lobong Ceremony, a community cleansing rite honouring the sea spirits that visitors can sometimes witness during Surin Islands trips.
quote: the Lobong Ceremony, held twice a year. It is the largest and most sacred ceremony of the Moken, symbolizing the cleansing of misfortune, the honoring of the sea

claim: Nam phrik takola, a Phang Nga speciality, is a roasted shrimp-paste relish pounded with kung siap (salt-cured skewered shrimp) and served with boiled and fresh vegetables.
quote: Nam Phrik Takola is a local Phang-Nga speciality, beginning with shrimp paste, roasted until fragrant, pounded in a mortar and pestle with kung siap (salt cured skewered shrimp) then served with boiled and fresh vegetables.

claim: Khao yam is a uniquely southern Thai rice salad of jasmine rice (often dyed blue with butterfly-pea flowers) tossed with toasted coconut, dried shrimp, fresh herbs and pungent budu fermented-fish-sauce dressing.
quote: khao yam is a rice salad tossed with toasted coconut, dried shrimp, herbs, and budu fish sauce... topped with an array of finely julienned fresh herbs, vegetables, and fruits, bound together with nam budu

claim: Southern Thailand's large Muslim population has shaped its breakfast culture around roti served with dal or curry, a direct inheritance from South Indian Muslim traders, and dishes like khao mok gai (turmeric chicken biryani) cooked with dry Indian spices.
quote: Roti canai arrives hot from the griddle, served with a bowl of dal or a golden curry: a direct inheritance from South Indian Muslim traders... Khao mok gai, a favourite of the south's large Muslim community

claim: Long Lae Sunday Market in Takua Thung district is regarded as the area's best non-tourist market — open Sundays 8am-5pm, mostly locals, with ~90% of stalls selling prepared southern Thai food alongside karaoke entertainment.
quote: It opens every Sunday from 08:00 am to 05:00 pm... best non-tourist market in the area... About 90% of the booths offer delicious prepared foods of all types. There are entertainment stages with one being karaoke.

claim: The Hong by Starlight tour, operating since 1989, is consistently rated 5/5 on Tripadvisor for paddling limestone hongs at sunset and floating krathongs after dark.
quote: Recent reviews describe the Hong by Starlight tour with John Gray's Sea Canoe as one of the most incredible experiences in Phuket, with everything well-organized, relaxing, and magical from start to finish.

claim: Sai Rung (Rainbow) Waterfall sits about 15 km north of Khao Lak near Pak Weep Beach, is free to enter, and is the most easily accessible waterfall in the area via a short walk from the parking lot.
quote: The Sai rung waterfall (rainbow waterfall) is admission free and the most easily accessible of all the waterfalls.

claim: Lampi Waterfall is a three-tier cascade inside Khao Lam Pi - Hat Thai Mueang National Park about 30 minutes south of Khao Lak, with swimming pools and rock jumping at the lowest tier.
quote: It is on three levels. At the bottom you can walk into the cool water and jump into the water from smaller rocks. The waterfall is located 30 minutes south of Khao Lak little bit before Thai Mueang village.

claim: Ton Pariwat Waterfall in Khao Lampi-Hat Thai Mueang National Park is reached via a 650-metre nature trail and flows year-round; late rainy season (October-December) is best for volume.
quote: To reach the waterfall, visitors must walk along a nature trail approximately 650 meters from the park entrance.

claim: Song Phraek River white-water rafting offers 5 km or 7 km runs through class II-IV rapids in Phang Nga jungle, roughly 100 km / two hours north of Phuket.
quote: Experience an action-packed 5 km or 7 km rafting adventure on the Songprak River in breathtaking Phang Nga province. You'll navigate class II to IV rapids through the stunning jungle.

claim: Peak water levels on the Song Phraek River fall between June and November, making this the recommended rafting window.
quote: The best season is June to November, when higher water levels create the most exciting rafting conditions.

claim: Khao Lak ATV / quad operators offer 30-minute to 2-hour jungle and waterfall trail rides, frequently bundled with bamboo rafting and elephant-sanctuary stops, with hotel pickup included.
quote: You can ride powerful ATVs through lush jungle trails, splash across rivers, and explore hidden natural spots with experienced guides.

claim: Khao Sok bamboo rafting on the Sok River (day-tripped from Khao Lak in Phang Nga) carries two guests per raft with a local captain and typically includes a riverbank stop for jungle coffee in a bamboo cup.
quote: During the bamboo raft journey, stops are made by the riverbank to boil water over an open fire for jungle coffee served in a bamboo cup.

claim: Khaolak Elephant Sanctuary stopped guest feeding programs from 2025, moving to observation-led ethical experiences, and was a runner-up in the Responsible Animal Welfare category in 2024 and 2025.
quote: Starting in 2025, Khaolak Elephant Sanctuary has officially stopped guest feeding programs, instead focusing on elephant welfare activities that allow elephants to express their natural behaviors.

claim: Khao Sok Elephant Sanctuary operates a strict observation-only, elephant-led model with no riding, no bathing and no physical contact with the rescued elephants.
quote: The sanctuary is home to rescued domestic elephants cared for by experienced mahouts, following strict observation-only, elephant-led principles, with no riding, no bathing, and no physical contact.

claim: Elephant Hills, Thailand's first luxury tented jungle camp, in Khao Sok National Park offers no-riding ethical elephant encounters and won the Responsible Animal Welfare Award in 2025.
quote: There are no elephant rides here. Instead, guests participate in meaningful interactions with rescued elephants in a sanctuary setting, supporting their welfare and long-term care.

claim: Green Elephant Sanctuary Park (Phuket, not Phang Nga) scores 4.9/5 on Tripadvisor with a no-riding, no-chains policy, but critics note its hands-on feeding/bathing model is less ethical than observation-only sanctuaries and the park was listed for sale in April 2025.
quote: The up-close interactivity that tourists love is not very ethical and is notably different from the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary.

claim: The Sea Turtle Conservation Festival runs annually in early March at Thai Mueang Beach, Phang Nga, with rehabilitated-turtle releases back into the Andaman as the centrepiece.
quote: The Sea Turtle Conservation Festival 2025 returns from March 1–10 at Thai Mueang Beach, Phang Nga.

claim: The Thai Muang Turtle Sanctuary (Phang Nga Coastal Fisheries Research and Development Centre) rears hatchlings in saltwater tanks until around eight months old before release; visitors can sponsor a release for about 3,000 baht.
quote: Young hatchlings are cared for in large saltwater tanks until they are around eight months old—an age at which their chances of survival in the wild increase significantly.

claim: HanumanWorld, Thailand's largest rainforest zipline park at 80,000 m2 of canopy, sits in Kathu, Phuket - not Phang Nga - so any zipline craving has to be planned as a Phuket side trip.
quote: Hanuman World is the biggest rainforest zip line park in Thailand, and it stands as Phuket's premier and largest rainforest zipline park, with an impressive 80,000 square meters of pristine jungle canopy.

claim: Phang Nga's peak/dry season runs November-April with November-March offering the most reliable weather; the southwest monsoon brings rain May-October with rougher seas.
quote: Peak season (November-March) provides most reliable weather but involves maximum crowds and pricing... The monsoon season, from May to October, sees heavier rainfall and rough seas, which can make boat trips more challenging.

claim: Phang Nga temperatures range 25-30 C during dry season with calm seas; humidity rises to 80-90% during monsoon vs 60-70% in dry months.
quote: the best time to visit Phang Nga Bay is during the dry season, from November to April, when the weather is sunny, and the sea is calm, with temperatures ranging from 25°C to 30°C

claim: Similan and Surin marine national parks both close May 15 - October 15 annually for monsoon safety and ecosystem recovery.
quote: the Similan and Surin marine national parks will close from May 15 to October 15 for monsoon safety and ecosystem recovery

claim: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) is mandatory for all foreign arrivals by air, land or sea in 2026 and must be submitted free via the official Thai Immigration portal within 72 hours of arrival.
quote: Submitting the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) via the official portal is completely free. Any website, agency or service charging a fee for TDAC is a scam

claim: TDAC replaced the paper TM6 form (discontinued May 2025) and failure to complete it can lead to boarding denial or immigration delays.
quote: It replaced the paper TM6 form, which was officially discontinued in May 2025... Failing to complete it can result in boarding denials or delays at immigration.

claim: Phuket Airport (HKT) to Khao Lak is about 70 km / 1 hour by private transfer (~$35-45), with no direct public transport; shared minivans and pre-booked taxis are the standard options.
quote: The fastest way to get from Phuket Airport to Khao Lak is by airport transfer, which takes 1 hour 7 minutes and costs $35-$45

claim: Krabi Airport (KBV) to Khao Lak is roughly 137 km / 2 hours by private car or minivan, with bus options taking 4+ hours via transfer.
quote: The distance between Krabi Airport and Khao Lak is approximately 137 km... By Private Car/Taxi: The fastest way is to drive, which takes 2h 1m

claim: Khao Lak works well as a base for Surin, Similan, Phang Nga Bay, James Bond Island and Khao Sok day trips; 5 nights is the recommended sweet spot to fit each headline attraction without rushing.
quote: 5 nights is recommended to give yourself time to explore the amazing Phang Nga bay, Khao Sok National Park and at least one of Similan or Surin Islands – each of those is a full-day trip in itself

claim: Phang Nga Bay sits about 25 km northeast of Phuket and is reachable in roughly 45 minutes by speedboat, making Phuket a viable day-trip base for the bay itself.
quote: Phang Nga Bay is located about 25 km northeast of Phuket, and most tours take around 45 minutes by speedboat to reach the main attractions

claim: In Phang Nga town there is no train; getting around uses songthaews (10-15 baht per ride, ~1,500 baht/day charter), motorbike rentals from ~300 baht/day and motorbike taxis (30-100 baht).
quote: There are a few public songthaews making the run up and down Phetkasem Rd, with most rides costing just 10 or 15B... Kean Tour, with an office right at the bus station, rents motorbikes for 300B per day

claim: Ao Phang Nga National Park charges 300 baht adult / 150 baht child; Similan and Surin marine parks charge 500 baht adult / 300 baht child for foreigners — Thai dual-pricing applies (Thais pay ~100 baht).
quote: Phang Nga Bay National Park - Adults: 300 Baht | Children: 150 Baht... Mu Koh Similan National Park - Adults: 500 Baht | Children: 300 Baht... Mu Koh Surin National Park - Foreign adults: 500 Baht | Foreign children: 300 Baht | Local adults: 100 Baht

claim: As of May 2026 the 60-day visa-free scheme still covers 93 countries (including US, UK, EU, Australia, Canada) but Thailand has announced plans to revert to a 57-country list, so travellers should verify status close to departure.
quote: Thailand plans to roll back its visa-free policy to a list of 57 eligible countries and territories, replacing the expanded 60-day exemption for 93 countries introduced in 2024

claim: Thailand has no strong tipping culture but small cash tips are appreciated: 20-40 baht or round-up at mid-range restaurants, ~10% at upscale places without service charge, 50-200 baht for massage/spa.
quote: At mid-range restaurants, leaving 20-40 baht or rounding up the bill is appreciated... At upscale restaurants, 10% is appropriate if service charge isn't already included. Tip 50-100 baht for a standard Thai massage

claim: Visa/Mastercard work at hotels, malls and large restaurants but markets, street food and small shops are cash-only; ATM withdrawals at Thai banks add a 150-220 baht fee per transaction and travellers should always choose THB billing to avoid DCC.
quote: Visa and Mastercard are widely accepted in hotels, malls, large restaurants, and supermarkets. Many smaller shops, markets, and street food stalls are cash-only... The fee per transaction can range between 150 and 220 Thai Baht
